sections.h2: Selling in a big city market
sections.html:
San Antonio sits at the head of the San Antonio River in Bexar County. Interstate 10, Interstates 35 and 37, Loop 410 and State Loop 1604 cut the city into very different pockets, and blocks inside and outside the loops can vary a lot in age, price and commute. A citywide average tells you little, so anchor your asking price to what sold close by.

  • Compare recent sales within a mile or two of your address.
  • Note whether the house is inside Loop 410, between the loops or beyond 1604.
  • Pull up the flood map when your lot backs onto the river or a creek.

Going through a broker rewards patience and a house in good repair. Investors fit better when the house needs work or your deadline is fixed.

San Antonio draws a wide range of buyers, so bids vary. A retail sale often produces the highest number, but it comes with inspections, showings and lender conditions. Skipping the agent saves the commission, but then the photos, the ads and the contracts are yours. Investors buy as-is on the date you pick, and they subtract repair and resale costs from what they offer. Line the bids up by what lands in your pocket once every cost is out.

  • Listing: the house is updated and the date can move.
  • Investor sale: a lien, an empty inherited house or tenant trouble.
  • Before signing, read who pays title, recording and repair credits.

sections.h2: Who sets value and who collects
sections.html:
Two offices touch your bill. BCAD puts the value on your property, and the Bexar County Tax Assessor-Collector is where the money goes. BCAD does not accept tax payments, so send payment questions to the assessor-collector.

For 2026, notices went to new owners and to owners whose value rose $1,000 or more, and a protest does not require a notice. Values are fixed as of January 1 across the state. Bills show up in October, and January 31 is the last day to pay without penalty. Every taxing unit on your lot sets its own rate, so your bill is the sum of several.

Six dates shape the year for a Bexar County owner.

Texas property tax schedule for Bexar County owners
DateWhat it means
January 1Valuation date and lien date
April 30Common exemption filing cutoff
May 15Usual protest deadline
July 20Review board approves appraisal records
September 29Deadline for most units to adopt rates
February 1Delinquency begins on unpaid taxes

The full list is on the Comptroller calendar.

Get the balance from the Bexar County Tax Assessor-Collector, then plan to clear it before closing day. Selling the house does not erase the lien.

An account that slips past January starts February with a 6 percent penalty and 1 percent interest. Come July the penalty is 12 percent, while interest continues to accrue. If collection lawyers get involved, up to a fifth more may be added. A homestead owner may ask for an installment plan, and some offices stretch it to 36 months. If the account goes to suit, a tax sale can follow, and the former owner can claim surplus proceeds for two years.

  • If you are appealing a value, pay at least the part nobody disputes.
  • Save each receipt.
  • Tell the closer about any plan in place, since the payoff figure depends on it.

Your main tool is the residence homestead exemption. Extra relief exists for age, for disability and for service-connected disability.

A school district takes $140,000 off a homestead's value, and another $60,000 comes off for owners who are seniors or disabled. Individual taxing units may add an exemption of their own, up to 20 percent of value but never under $5,000. A yearly 10 percent cap limits how fast a homestead's appraised value can grow. Depending on rating, a service-disabled owner gets $5,000 to $12,000 off, and at 100 percent the entire homestead is exempt. An heir missing from the recorded deed brings an affidavit, a death certificate and a recent utility bill.

You can remove someone who stays after being told to go through a justice court case. Property Code chapter 24B also lets you ask the sheriff or constable to act, but only in narrow cases.

The shortcut applies only when the person refused to leave, the property was closed to the public at entry, no suit is pending between the two of you, and the occupant is no relative and no past or present tenant. An owner who removes someone wrongly can be sued. Tenants normally receive three days' notice. The writ of possession cannot go out until six days after judgment. Some investors will buy with the occupant still inside and deal with it themselves, which spares you the wait.

Your deed gets recorded with the Bexar County clerk, after a notary or comparable officer witnesses the signature. Recording costs $5.00 for page one and $4.00 for each page after, with other records fees on top. In most sales the title company handles the filing.

Heirs have several routes to clear title. The right one depends on what the owner left and what the house owes.

With a will, the executor or an heir files it for probate, which Texas permits for four years after death. When no administration is needed, the muniment of title order and the will get recorded with the county clerk. No will? A small estate affidavit can serve for modest estates. A deed naming a beneficiary and recorded before the owner's death moves the house outside probate, and a Lady Bird deed lets the owner keep selling rights while alive. Expect the closer to ask for whichever paper applies.

  • Order certified copies of the death certificate.
  • Find the last recorded deed for the parcel.
  • Ask the appraisal district about the homestead exemption before the next tax year.

Most Texas mortgages allow a sale without a court case, so the clock runs fast.

Under federal rules a servicer generally cannot begin until the home loan is over 120 days past due. A default notice then opens a 20 day period to bring the loan current. At least 21 days before the auction, the sale notice has to be mailed, posted at the courthouse and filed with the clerk. The auction falls on a first Tuesday. If that Tuesday lands on January 1 or July 4, it moves to the Wednesday. Selling before the date can preserve equity and spare you a foreclosure on your record.

Your bill is a stack of separate rates, one for each taxing unit that touches your lot, so two houses a mile apart can owe quite different amounts. Pull the BCAD record for your parcel and read it line by line: the value, the exemptions on file and the units listed. A buyer from out of town may not know that Bexar County values are fixed on January 1 while bills do not arrive until October. Explain that gap, and give the figure from the assessor-collector rather than a guess. Where a protest is pending, say so, because a lower value would change what the buyer carries.

Inside Loop 410 you may be selling a house of real age, with older wiring and plumbing that an inspector will flag. Between the loops and out toward 1604, buyers expect newer systems and will compare lots and commutes. Say plainly which kind of block you are on, and match your bid requests to it. An investor who knows the area will price the roof and the foundation within minutes, so a seller who has already priced them avoids a long haggle. Photos of recent work and any warranty papers speak louder than adjectives.

If you go with a cash buyer, line up a few things early. Carry your photo ID, your deed or inheritance papers and the newest tax statement. Have the title company quote you a payoff on every lien. Get the closing date in writing. Read the settlement statement ahead of time so each fee has a name beside it.

faqs.q: Which office collects San Antonio property tax?
faqs.a: Payments go to the Bexar County Tax Assessor-Collector. The Bexar Central Appraisal District does not take them.

faqs.q: Do I need a notice to protest my value in San Antonio?
faqs.a: No. You can file a protest without a notice. Check any notice you get for the cutoff, which most years falls in mid May.

faqs.q: What homestead exemption do school districts give?
faqs.a: School districts deduct $140,000 from the value, plus $60,000 more when the owner is a senior or disabled.

faqs.q: What happens to the lien when a San Antonio house sells?
faqs.a: The lien stays attached, so the title company pays any old tax from your proceeds at closing.

faqs.q: When do foreclosure auctions occur near San Antonio?
faqs.a: On a first Tuesday, during daytime hours, after a sale notice at least three weeks earlier.
